final.summary: Recommended: fused. Peak 90th pct core temp 37.97 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.02 °C, 45% of priority-weighted work done.
reasons: **We're right at the heat limit.** This plan keeps the crew just barely under the safe body-heat level, with almost no room to spare. If it gets hotter than expected or anyone feels dizzy, sick, or confused, stop work and get them cooled down right away.

**Everyone comes inside from 1 to 3 pm.** Lightning and severe thunderstorms are expected, so no outdoor work then. Because of that break and the heat, we'll finish a bit under half of today's work, with the most important jobs done first.

**Kofi stays off the heaviest jobs while it's hot.** He's new and his body isn't used to this heat yet. We could keep him on light work all day for a bigger safety cushion, but we'd only finish about a third of the work. Another plan we looked at had the same heat risk and got less done, so this one is the best balance.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.

calls.prompt:
Write 3 short plain-language bullet points (no jargon) for a crew lead explaining this schedule's trade-offs. Facts:
Peak 90th pct core temp 37.97 °C (limit 38.0), tightest margin 0.02 °C, 45% of priority-weighted work done.
No outdoor work 13:00-15:00 (lightning, severe_thunderstorm).
Kofi (new hire) is not acclimatized: no very heavy work in high heat.
Alternatives: optimizer:throughput (42% work, peak 37.96 °C); llm-idea:Keep the new hire on light work only (30% work, peak 37.78 °C)
calls.response:
- **We're right at the heat limit.** This plan keeps the crew just barely under the safe body-heat level, with almost no room to spare. If it gets hotter than expected or anyone feels dizzy, sick, or confused, stop work and get them cooled down right away.

- **Everyone comes inside from 1 to 3 pm.** Lightning and severe thunderstorms are expected, so no outdoor work then. Because of that break and the heat, we'll finish a bit under half of today's work, with the most important jobs done first.

- **Kofi stays off the heaviest jobs while it's hot.** He's new and his body isn't used to this heat yet. We could keep him on light work all day for a bigger safety cushion, but we'd only finish about a third of the work. Another plan we looked at had the same heat risk and got less done, so this one is the best balance.
